p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The unprecedented surge of retail investors entering India’s capital markets, fueled by discount brokerages and mobile investment applications, has democratized a financial terrain once dominated by institutional elites. This digital wave has funneled domestic savings away from traditional low-yield assets like gold and fixed deposits directly into equity markets, providing vital capital to Indian enterprises. However, this rapid financialization introduces severe systemic risks, primarily driven by the behavioral vulnerabilities of inexperienced investors. Many new entrants treat equity markets as speculative spaces, engaging in high-risk options trading and leveraged intraday bets driven by unverified social media influencers. This trend is worsened by a complete lack of financial literacy regarding market cycles, valuation metrics, and risk management practices. A sharp market correction could lead to severe capital losses for millions of middle-class households, damaging long-term faith in the financial system. Securing this retail investment wave requires strong regulations on financial influencers, mandatory risk disclosure tools on trading apps, and deep systemic efforts to turn speculative traders into long-term, informed investors.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Depending on what and how you communicate with others or conduct yourself, you will either draw people close to you or drive them away from you. The largest content of non-verbal communication is contributed by what is popularly called body language. Depending on what this speaks you would get a red-carpet welcome or rejection. Hence, it is important to know where you stand. It is equally important to know the requirements of different situations, time and place to ensure you are able to take care of your own acceptance. In a tradition-ruled country like India, body conduct has an important relevance in valuing relationships and individuals. If your general disposition is good you will readily emit sparks that make you the centre of happenings. Expression of the eye, good eye contact makes your interlocutor feel you are keen to live life. Sensitive people keep changing their expression and literally swing up or down.

sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

questions.q: The entry of retail investors into India's capital markets was mainly accelerated by:
opts: Discount brokerages and mobile investment apps.
Institutions giving up control of equity.
Laws banning individual ownership of gold.
questions.why: Detail: the first sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A positive economic outcome of this surge, according to the text, is:
opts: Domestic savings flowing into equity and providing capital to enterprises.
questions.why: Detail: the second sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author is concerned that many inexperienced investors view the stock market as:
opts: A conservative arena for preserving wealth.
A speculative playground driven by social-media advice.
questions.why: Detail: the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The word "democratized" in the first sentence means that the market has been:
opts: made open and accessible to ordinary people
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: once 'dominated by institutional elites', it is now open to retail investors. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the final sentence, protecting new retail investors requires:
opts: Regulating financial influencers and adding risk-disclosure tools to apps.
questions.why: Detail: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, a warm social welcome depends mainly on one's
questions.why: Detail: 'Depending on what this [body language] speaks you would get a red-carpet welcome or rejection'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: What is particularly significant in a country like India for being socially accepted, as the passage implies?
questions.why: Detail: 'In a tradition-ruled country like India, body conduct has an important relevance'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which phrase in the passage means "warm and willing acceptance"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: The word "interlocutor" in the passage means
questions.why: Vocabulary: the person you are speaking with. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Consider: (i) It is important to know how good or bad one's body language is. (ii) Responding to the time, place and situation helps decide one's acceptance. According to the passage:
questions.why: Both are stated: 'know where you stand' and 'know the requirements of different situations, time and place'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ______ wear a helmet; it is the law.”
questions.why: 'Must' expresses obligation. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the camp.”
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + verb. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is fond ______ classical music.”
questions.why: 'Fond of'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the error: “Neither of the two answers are correct.”
questions.why: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb: 'is correct'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The committee will announce the results tomorrow.”
opts: The results will be announce by the committee tomorrow.
The results will announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results would be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
questions.why: Future passive: will be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
questions.why: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session in Bombay.

questions.q: Engineers' Day (15 September) is observed on the birth anniversary of:
questions.why: Static.

questions.q: Gandhi's Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from:
questions.why: Against the salt tax.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for sodium is:
questions.why: From the Latin 'natrium'.

questions.q: The Living Planet Report 2026 is released by:
Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.why: Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana crossed 1 crore registrations in 2026. It promotes:
Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), observed on 31 October, marks the birth anniversary of:
questions.why: Observed since 2014.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.why: India's Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in 2014.

questions.q: How many Lok Sabha seats does Goa have?
questions.why: North Goa and South Goa. Goa has 40 assembly seats and 1 Rajya Sabha seat.

questions.q: Ramesh walks 9 km towards the north, turns right and walks 12 km. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles, so the distance is the hypotenuse: the square root of 81 + 144 = 225, which is 15 km.

questions.q: Pointing to a woman, Rohan said, "She is the only daughter of my mother's father." How is the woman related to Rohan?
questions.why: His mother's father is his maternal grandfather. That man's only daughter is Rohan's mother.

questions.q: Odometer is to distance as barometer is to:
questions.why: An odometer measures distance travelled; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: Rice, wheat and maize are cereal grains. Cotton is a fibre crop.

questions.q: Book is to library as painting is to:
questions.why: Books are kept and shown in a library; paintings in a gallery.

questions.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.why: The only daughter of her father is the woman herself, so the man is her husband.

questions.q: Town P is 12 km due north of town Q. Town R is 5 km due west of P. What is the shortest distance between Q and R?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles: the square root of 144 + 25 = 169, which is 13 km.

questions.q: Sarpanch is to Panchayat as Mayor is to:
questions.why: A Sarpanch heads a Panchayat; a Mayor heads a Municipal Corporation.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?
questions.why: The terms are 1x2, 2x3, 3x4 and so on. The next is 7 x 8 = 56.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 8, 27, 64, 125, ?
questions.why: These are the cubes of 2, 3, 4 and 5. The next is 6 cubed, 216.

questions.q: The fundamental cause of most chronic diseases, according to Hahnemann, is:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psora, sycosis or syphilis.

questions.q: Destructive ulceration, bone pains worse at night and a tendency to deformity are features of which miasm?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Syphilis: destruction and ulceration, night aggravation.

questions.q: The word 'dynamis' in homoeopathic philosophy refers to:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The spirit-like power animating the body.

questions.q: Aggravation from the slightest motion, with relief from pressure and from lying on the painful side, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Bryonia is worse from any motion and better from pressure. Rhus tox has the opposite modality, better from continued motion.

questions.q: Prolapse of the uterus with bearing-down sensation as if everything would come out, crossing the legs for relief, with indifference to family, indicates:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sepia: bearing down, indifference to loved ones.

questions.q: Complaints from loss of vital fluids (haemorrhage, diarrhoea, lactation), with periodicity and great sensitivity to touch, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. China: weakness from loss of fluids.

questions.q: Thirst for large quantities of cold water at long intervals, stitching pains worse from the slightest motion, and irritability with a wish to be left alone suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Bryonia: large drinks at long intervals.

questions.q: Globules used in homoeopathy are made of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Sugar-of-milk is used for triturations and tablets; globules are cane sugar.

questions.q: In the decimal scale, the first potency (1X) has a drug-to-vehicle ratio of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. One part drug to nine parts vehicle.

questions.q: The first and last chapters of Kent's Repertory are:
questions.why: The repertory runs from Mind to Generalities.

questions.q: A rubric in a repertory is:
opts: a heading under which remedies producing that symptom are listed
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The basic unit of a repertory.

questions.q: Claw hand is classically due to a lesion of the:
questions.why: Ulnar claw from paralysis of the interossei and medial lumbricals.

questions.q: The cardiac output equals:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About 5 L/min at rest.

questions.q: The cardinal signs of inflammation described by Celsus are rubor, tumor, calor and:
questions.why: Virchow later added loss of function.

questions.q: Kala-azar is transmitted by the:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Leishmania donovani; LD bodies in splenic aspirate.

questions.q: The most specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial infarction is:
questions.why: Cardiac troponin I or T.

questions.q: The commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. The pneumococcus.

questions.q: Fever, pain in the right hypochondrium and arrest of inspiration on palpation under the right costal margin (Murphy's sign) suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Murphy's sign is the classic sign of acute cholecystitis.

questions.q: The commonest cause of infantile diarrhoea worldwide is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotavirus vaccine is in India's UIP.

questions.q: The first stage of labour ends with:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. First stage: from true labour pains to full dilatation.

questions.q: After a clean surgical incision, with smarting pain and a sense of insult, the remedy usually indicated is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Staphysagria: clean-cut wounds and post-operative pain.

questions.q: A partial-thickness burn with blisters is classed as:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Full-thickness burns are painless and need grafting.

questions.q: Post-mortem staining (livor mortis, hypostasis) is due to:
opts: gravitational pooling of blood in dependent parts
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Begins within about 1–2 hours of death.

questions.q: Genus epidemicus is used in outbreak control to:
opts: find a common remedy for most cases in an epidemic
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Found by studying the symptoms of several cases.

questions.q: Biomedical waste in India is segregated by colour-coded bags. Human anatomical waste goes into the:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Yellow category: anatomical, soiled and chemical waste for incineration.
